aboutPreview.title: About Me
aboutPreview.text: A clinical psychologist with experience in public and private practice, I work with individuals, couples, and families. Training as a systemic-relational psychotherapist, I believe that change is born from relationships and the resources each person brings.

about.title: Ida Sato
about.subtitle: Clinical Psychologist — Order of Psychologists of Veneto, no. 13939
about.bio: I'm a clinical psychologist registered with the Veneto Psychologists' Register (no. 13939), working in private practice in Meledo (VI) and Spinea (VE). My experience was built in public services and the social-private sector: I worked as a school psychologist in ULSS 6 Padova schools, led parenting support groups, and collaborated with therapeutic communities and child development services. I currently also serve as head of educational and psychological services at Cooperativa FAI in Padova. I'm specializing in systemic-relational psychotherapy at the Centro Padovano di Terapia della Famiglia. This approach guides my work: every person is part of a network of relationships, and change happens when we learn to see and use the resources within us and around us.

approach.title: My approach
approach.text: I work with a systemic-relational approach: I look not only at the person, but also at the relationships they're immersed in — family, couple, school, work. I don't believe in one-size-fits-all solutions: every path begins with listening and is built together, at your own pace. My goal is to help you recognize the resources you already have and find new ways to feel better in your relationships.

empathy.title: Listening
empathy.text: Every journey begins with listening. I welcome your experience without judgment, paying attention to what you say and what you can't yet put into words.

respect.title: Respect
respect.text: Your pace is the right pace. I don't rush the process and I respect your choices, working with you, not in your place.

professionalism.title: Professionalism
professionalism.text: I train continuously, participate in regular supervision, and work with an evidence-based approach. I've published research in international journals such as Psychiatry Research and Stigma and Health.

servicesPreview.title: My Services
servicesPreview.subtitle: I offer various psychological paths to accompany you on your journey to well-being.

services.title: My Services
services.subtitle: Each path is tailor-made to meet your specific needs.

individual.title: Individual psychological support
individual.description: A space dedicated to you, to face anxiety, stress, moments of crisis, or simply the need to better understand what you're going through. Together we build a tailored path, at your own pace.

extendedDescription.p1: Individual psychological support is a safe, private space where you can explore what you feel, name your difficulties, and discover resources you didn't know you had.
extendedDescription.p2: I use a systemic-relational approach: this means I look not only at you in isolation, but also at the context of relationships you live in — family, work, friendships — because that's often where both the struggles and the possibilities for change are found.
extendedDescription.p3: Every path is different: together we define realistic goals and work at your pace, without pressure.

benefits.b1: Greater awareness of your emotions and how you relate to others
benefits.b2: Concrete strategies for managing anxiety, stress, and difficult moments
benefits.b3: Greater confidence in yourself and your abilities
benefits.b4: New resources for facing life changes and transitions

s1.title: First contact
s1.text: You write or call me to briefly tell me what's bringing you to seek help. We find a time to meet, with no commitment.

s2.title: First session
s2.text: We meet for about 50 minutes — at my office in Meledo (VI) or Spinea (VE), or online. We get to know each other and assess together whether it makes sense to start a path.

s3.title: Personalized path
s3.text: We define concrete goals and a sustainable frequency (weekly or bi-weekly). We regularly reassess how things are going.

f1.question: How long does an individual support path last?
f1.answer: There's no predefined duration: it depends on your goals and how the path evolves. Some conclude in a few weeks, others take longer. We discuss it openly from the very first meeting.

f2.question: Do I need to have a serious problem to seek support?
f2.answer: No. Psychological support is also helpful during times of change, uncertainty, or simply when you feel the need for a space to reflect.

f3.question: Is individual support suitable for teenagers?
f3.answer: For minors, I offer a dedicated service with age-appropriate methods. Individual support is designed for adults aged 18 and over.

couples.title: Couples and family counseling
couples.description: When communication breaks down or an important change tests the relationship — a separation, a birth, a loss — a neutral space can make all the difference. I work with couples and families to find a way to talk and be together again.

extendedDescription.p1: Couple and family relationships go through difficult moments that sometimes can't be managed alone. Counseling offers a neutral space where each person can express themselves and feel heard.
extendedDescription.p2: With a systemic-relational approach, we explore together the dynamics that have developed and look for new balances. You don't need to be in crisis to ask for help: sometimes just wanting to better understand how your relationship works is enough.
extendedDescription.p3: In my experience with families and couples, I've seen that change is possible when people learn to listen to each other differently.

benefits.b1: Rediscovering a way to communicate and truly listen to each other
benefits.b2: Learning to manage conflicts without them becoming destructive
benefits.b3: Better understanding of the dynamics that have developed in the relationship
benefits.b4: Support during times of change — births, separations, losses

s1.title: First contact
s1.text: One partner or family member contacts me. We talk briefly to understand the situation and schedule a first meeting.

s2.title: Introductory meeting
s2.text: The first session is with all members involved. Everyone has space to share their point of view in a safe, neutral environment.

s3.title: Shared path
s3.text: We define goals together. Sessions involve all participants, with the possibility of individual meetings when helpful.

f1.question: Do both partners need to agree to come?
f1.answer: Ideally yes. If your partner is uncertain, we can have a first session together to see if the path could be helpful — with no obligation.

f2.question: Can I have family counseling with my children?
f2.answer: Yes, we assess together who it's helpful to involve and how, based on the specific situation.

f3.question: Is couples counseling only for couples in crisis?
f3.answer: No. It's also useful for those who want to improve communication, face an important change, or invest in the quality of their relationship.

school.title: School psychology
school.description: Affective and sex education programs in schools, support for students with SEN and SLD, and counseling for teachers and parents. I bring to schools the experience gained in public services.

extendedDescription.p1: I worked as a school psychologist in primary and secondary schools in ULSS 6 Padova, delivering affective and sex education programs. This experience in public services taught me how fundamental school is as an environment for young people's well-being.
extendedDescription.p2: Today I continue to collaborate with schools through classroom projects, individual support for students with learning difficulties (SEN and SLD), and counseling for teachers and parents.
extendedDescription.p3: My approach is always collaborative: I work closely with families and school staff to build tailored interventions.

benefits.b1: Promoting emotional and relational well-being in the classroom
benefits.b2: Targeted support for students with SEN and SLD
benefits.b3: Concrete tools for teachers in managing group dynamics
benefits.b4: Strengthening collaboration between school and family

s1.title: Needs assessment
s1.text: I meet with school leadership and teachers to understand the specific needs of the school and its students.

s2.title: Design
s2.text: I create a tailored project: classroom workshops, listening services, teacher training, or individual support.

s3.title: Intervention and monitoring
s3.text: I carry out the interventions and monitor results, maintaining constant dialogue with teachers and parents.

f1.question: Who can request a school psychology intervention?
f1.answer: School leadership, teachers, or parents. In any case, I work involving all relevant figures.

f2.question: What kind of classroom activities are offered?
f2.answer: Interactive workshops on affective and sex education, emotional management, peer relationships, and bullying prevention. Always adapted to the students' age.

f3.question: How is a student with SLD supported?
f3.answer: Through assessing difficulties, collaborating with family and teachers for personalized teaching strategies, and when needed, individual tutoring. I have specific training as an SLD and SEN tutor.

parenting.title: Parenting support
parenting.description: Being a parent of adolescents and pre-adolescents means facing new challenges every day: conflicts, anxiety, social media, demands for autonomy. A dedicated path helps you find your own way to be there.

extendedDescription.p1: I led parenting support groups at ULSS 6 Padova, working with parents of adolescents and pre-adolescents on topics like adolescent changes, anxiety and depressive disorders, hikikomori, conflict, and autonomy.
extendedDescription.p2: This experience confirmed for me that parents don't need recipes, but a space to reflect together on their role.
extendedDescription.p3: With a systemic-relational approach, I look at the family as a whole: understanding family dynamics helps find more effective strategies and strengthen the bond with your children.

benefits.b1: Better understanding what your children are going through at different stages of growth
benefits.b2: Concrete strategies for managing conflicts and family tensions
benefits.b3: Strengthening the bond with your children, based on listening and trust
benefits.b4: Finding a balance between rules, boundaries, and autonomy

s1.title: First contact
s1.text: You briefly tell me about the situation and we figure out together whether parenting support is the most suitable path.

s2.title: Initial meeting
s2.text: In the first session, we explore family dynamics and the difficulties you're experiencing. One or both parents can attend.

s3.title: Support path
s3.text: We work through regular meetings on the concrete challenges that arise, developing new resources for your role as a parent.

f1.question: Is parenting support only for parents in difficulty?
f1.answer: No. It's useful for anyone who wants to better understand family dynamics, improve communication with their children, or face a phase of change.

f2.question: Do both parents need to participate?
f2.answer: Not necessarily. You can work with one parent alone. When possible, involving both leads to better results.

f3.question: What age range is it recommended for?
f3.answer: Any stage, from childhood to adolescence. The challenges change with age and the path adapts accordingly.

youth.title: Support for children and adolescents
youth.description: Psychological support for children and young people experiencing emotional difficulties, anxiety, insecurity, or struggling in peer relationships. A path designed for their age, with family involvement.

extendedDescription.p1: Childhood and adolescence are phases of great transformation, and sometimes young people need extra help to face them. Through my internship at the Child Development Service of ULSS 6 and my work with educational communities, I gained experience working with minors with developmental disorders, emotional difficulties, and anxiety.
extendedDescription.p2: With younger children, I use age-appropriate tools — play, drawing, expressive activities. With adolescents, dialogue is central.
extendedDescription.p3: In both cases, the family is an active part of the path, because a child's or teenager's well-being is never built in isolation.

benefits.b1: A safe space to express emotions and difficulties without judgment
benefits.b2: Development of emotional and relational skills appropriate for their age
benefits.b3: Support in facing changes at school, in the family, and with peers
benefits.b4: Active involvement of parents for an integrated path

s1.title: Meeting with parents
s1.text: The first step is a session with parents to understand the situation and concerns. It helps me get a complete picture before meeting the child or teenager.

s2.title: Meeting with the child
s2.text: I meet the child or teenager in a welcoming environment, using age-appropriate methods — play, drawing, or dialogue — to build a trusting relationship.

s3.title: Integrated path
s3.text: The work continues with regular sessions with the child and periodic meetings with parents, for coordinated support.

f1.question: From what age can a child start a path?
f1.answer: From about 6 years of age. For younger children, the work is mainly with parents through parenting support.

f2.question: Are parents present during sessions?
f2.answer: It depends on the age. With younger children, parents may be involved. With teenagers, sessions are individual, with periodic meetings with parents.

f3.question: Is the school involved in the path?
f3.answer: Only when helpful and with parental consent. Collaboration with teachers can be very effective for coordinated support.

online.title: Online sessions
online.description: Remote psychological consultations via video call, with the same care and confidentiality as in-office sessions. Ideal for those with irregular schedules, who live far away, or prefer the comfort of home.

extendedDescription.p1: Online sessions take place via video call on secure platforms and are fully equivalent to in-office sessions. Scientific research confirms their effectiveness.
extendedDescription.p2: In my experience, they work particularly well for those who have difficulty traveling, inflexible work schedules, or simply prefer the comfort of a familiar space. All I ask is a stable connection and an environment where you can talk freely.
extendedDescription.p3: You can alternate between online and in-person sessions based on your needs.

benefits.b1: You can participate from anywhere with an internet connection
benefits.b3: Same quality and confidentiality as in-office sessions
benefits.b4: Ideal for those with inflexible schedules or who live far away

s1.title: Booking
s1.text: Contact me to schedule an online appointment. I'll send you the video call link before the session.

s2.title: Preparation
s2.text: You need a stable connection, a device with camera and microphone, and a quiet place where you can speak privately.

s3.title: The session
s3.text: We connect at the agreed time. The session lasts about 50 minutes, just like in the office. Payment is made by bank transfer.

f1.question: What platform is used for video calls?
f1.answer: I use secure platforms that comply with privacy regulations. I'll share the details when you book your appointment.

f2.question: Are online sessions as effective as in-office ones?
f2.answer: Yes. Scientific research confirms that online sessions are equally effective as in-person ones for most situations.

f3.question: Can I alternate between online and in-office sessions?
f3.answer: Of course. Many people choose a mixed approach, alternating based on their needs.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions about psychological counseling.

q1.question: How does the first consultation work?
q1.answer: The first session lasts about 50 minutes and is an introductory meeting: you tell me what brings you here, I explain how I work, and together we assess whether it makes sense to start a path. It's a chance to get to know each other, with no obligation to continue. You can choose to meet at my office in Meledo (VI) or Spinea (VE), or via video call.

q2.question: How long is a session?
q2.answer: There's no fixed duration: it depends on what you bring and the goals we set together. Some paths conclude in a few weeks, others take longer. From the very first meeting, we discuss this openly and periodically reassess how things are going, so you always know where we stand.

q3.question: What is the cost of sessions?
q3.answer: The cost varies depending on the type of path (individual, couple, family). I'll let you know during the first phone or email contact, before scheduling an appointment, so you can decide at your own pace. Psychological sessions are tax-deductible as healthcare expenses in Italy.

q4.question: Are online sessions available?
q4.answer: Yes, online sessions take place via video call on secure platforms and are equivalent to in-office sessions in quality and confidentiality. They work well for those who have difficulty traveling, inflexible schedules, or simply prefer to stay at home. You can also alternate between in-person and online sessions based on your needs.

q5.question: How can I book an appointment?
q5.answer: You can write to me by email, WhatsApp, or fill out the form on the Contact page. You can also call me directly. I usually reply within 24 hours on working days. In the first contact, you briefly tell me what's bringing you to seek help, so I can understand if I'm the right professional for you.

q6.question: Are sessions confidential?
q6.answer: Yes, confidentiality is a fundamental right and a professional obligation. As a psychologist, I'm bound by professional secrecy under the Italian Psychologists' Code of Ethics (articles 11-17). Everything that emerges during sessions is strictly confidential, both in the office and online.

q7.question: What is the difference between a psychologist and a psychotherapist?
q7.answer: A psychologist holds a master's degree and is registered with the professional board; they can provide prevention, diagnosis, support, and psychological rehabilitation. A psychotherapist has an additional 4-year specialization that qualifies them to use specific therapeutic techniques. I'm a psychologist and I'm specializing in systemic-relational psychotherapy at the Centro Padovano di Terapia della Famiglia. My work is already guided by this approach, which looks at the person in the context of their relationships.

q8.question: How do I know if I need psychological support?
q8.answer: You don't need to have a 'serious' problem to ask for help. If you're struggling, if a recurring thought won't leave you alone, if the relationships around you have become complicated, or if you simply feel the need for a space to reflect — these are all valid reasons. The first session is there precisely to understand together whether a path could be helpful, with no commitment.

q9.question: Are sessions tax-deductible?
q9.answer: Yes. Psychological services are tax-deductible healthcare expenses in Italy at 19%. I issue a regular invoice after each session and, if needed, an annual summary for your accountant.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes how personal data collected through this website is processed, in accordance with EU Regulation 2016/679 (GDPR).

controller.title: Data Controller
controller.text: The data controller is Ida Sato, VAT {piva}, based in {address}. For any request regarding personal data, you can write to {email}.

legalBasis.title: Legal Basis for Processing
legalBasis.text: Personal data is processed on the following legal bases: data subject's consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) for data submitted through the contact form; controller's legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) for anonymous traffic analysis and site operation; performance of pre-contractual measures (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) for handling consultation requests.

dataCollected.title: Data Collected
dataCollected.text: Through the contact form, we collect: name, email address, phone number (optional), and message text. This data is used exclusively to respond to inquiries received. Blog content is delivered through the Sanity CDN (cdn.sanity.io), which may log standard HTTP request data (IP address, user-agent). Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR for the contact form; Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR for website content delivery.

thirdParty.title: Third-Party Services
thirdParty.text: This site uses the following third-party services: Vercel Inc. (vercel.com) for website hosting and traffic analysis; Sanity AS (sanity.io) for managing and delivering blog content via the CDN cdn.sanity.io. Both providers operate in compliance with the GDPR and have appropriate Data Processing Agreements (DPA) in place. For more information, please refer to their respective privacy policies.

analytics.title: Traffic Analysis
analytics.text: This site uses Vercel Analytics and Vercel Speed Insights to collect anonymous usage data. These tools do not use cookies, do not collect personally identifiable information, and do not perform cross-site tracking. Data is processed within the European Union and is not transferred to third countries. Vercel Analytics is GDPR-compliant.

cookies.title: Cookies and Local Storage
cookies.text: This site exclusively uses technical cookies necessary for operation. Additionally, the site uses the browser's localStorage (not technically a cookie) to store theme preference (light/dark) and language selection. This data remains exclusively on your device and is not transmitted to third parties. No profiling or third-party cookies are used. Since no profiling cookies are present, a cookie consent banner is not required.

retention.title: Data Retention
retention.text: Data collected through the contact form is retained only for the time strictly necessary to handle the request and is subsequently deleted. Anonymous analytics data cannot be traced back to individuals and is retained according to Vercel's policies.

rights.title: Your Rights
rights.text: Under the GDPR, you have the right to access your data, request its rectification or deletion, restrict processing, and object to it. To exercise these rights, contact us at {email}. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italian Data Protection Authority) at www.garanteprivacy.it.
